outcome_statement: On every counted deal in the window, the node's own records show it came through on the terms it accepted: it paid as agreed when it bought, and when it provided, it recorded settlement for every invoice it issued and reported running the model it was asked for. Every record is checked against the signer keys the reader trusts. A deal that holds a record whose signature does not verify (altered, or not what it claims), or whose signer is not among those keys, is shown as "Couldn't tell" (not_evaluable), never as met or not met; the run's result records which. A signer outside your keys is not a finding of tampering. A record that does not verify never creates a deal, so with no trusted keys there is no deal to report and the run says so. A row is countersigned only when the book also holds the other side's own signed leg of every payment and that leg's signature verifies under a key you trust; otherwise it stays self-attested, and the result says whether that leg's signature did not verify (altered, or not what it claims) or the other side signed with a key you have not chosen to trust, which alone is not a sign of tampering. To earn countersigned, give your trusted keys again with the other side's key added (capsulectl profile update --profile <your profile> --trusted-key <your key> --trusted-key <the other side's key>: the flag replaces the list).
resolution_rule: a deal is resolved only when every term that applies to it is met
counterparty_note: The peer's book of the same exchange is not held on this node. It is shown as not_available, never as a failure or as agreement.

clauses.check_question: Did the node come through on the terms it accepted?
clauses.label: Paid as agreed
clauses.claim: When the node bought, every invoice it saw has a settlement its own wallet reported, for the invoice's amount. Every record is verified under the reader's trusted keys first. A deal with a record whose signature does not verify, or whose signer is not among those keys, reads "Couldn't tell", and the two reasons are told apart; a signer outside your keys is not a finding of tampering.

clauses.check_question: Did the node come through on the terms it accepted?
clauses.label: Settlement recorded for every invoice it issued
clauses.claim: When the node provided, its records show the exchange it accepted terms for, and every invoice it issued has a settlement its wallet reported, for the invoice's amount. This does not show that the answer was good, or that the node's own report of what it ran is true. Records are verified under the reader's trusted keys, as for the term above. The grade countersigned also needs the other side's own signed leg of each payment to verify under a key you trust.

clauses.check_question: Did the node come through on the terms it accepted?
clauses.label: Model it reports running matches the model requested (its own record, or a referee's ruling)
clauses.claim: When the node provided and a referee decided the deal, this row shows the referee's verdict, read for this node as the node's own verdict counts read it (corroborated, or contradicted naming the other half, is met; contradicted naming this node is not_met; anything else reads "Couldn't tell"); a deal a referee already adjudicated is not judged again. Otherwise it compares the model its record says was requested with the model its record says answered, which no one else has checked and no verifier can check against the accepted terms, since those carry the model only inside their digest.
